newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RBA says satisfied with Morgan role on gold sales.
newsitem.headline: RBA says satisfied with Morgan role on gold sales.

text.p: Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) governor Ian Macfarlane said in a statement on Thursday that he is satisfied that WMC Ltd managing director Hugh Morgan has fulfilled his obligations as a member of the RBA board.

Macfarlane issued a statement in response to media reports raising the possiblity of conflicts of interest for private sector members of the Reserve Bank board, particularly in connection with the central bank's sales of gold in the first half of 1997.

"It is inevitable that potential conflicts will arise from time to time for members of a Board which has the responsibility to make decisions affecting the economy as a whole, as well as particular sectors of the economy," Macfarlane said.

"This is a consequence of the longstanding arrangements in Australia which seek to bring a range of commercial and other private sector expertise and knowledge to bear on the central bank's policy-making.

"It would make the Board of the Bank unworkable if members had to absent themselves from all discussions and decisions which potentially gave rise to conflicts of interest with their other activities," he added.

Macfarlane said that in appointing Board members, the Bank selected people judged to have high ethical standards able to dissociate their personal and business interests from the national interests with which the Bank was concerned.
Members also signed a secrecy declaration preventing them from using information gained in their position on the Board in their outside roles.
"On the basis of my discuss of my discussions with Mr Morgan, and the statement he issued today, I am satisfied that Mr Morgan has fulfilled his obligation as a Board member," Macfarlane concluded.
